items.stem: Which is the definition of capacitance?
options: the charge stored per unit time
the charge stored per unit potential difference
the energy stored per unit charge
the potential difference per unit charge
items.answer: the charge stored per unit potential difference
items.markingKey: C = Q/V.

items.stem: Derive the formula for the combined capacitance of two capacitors in parallel.
items.answer: Same p.d. V across each; total charge Q = Q₁ + Q₂ = C₁V + C₂V, so C = Q/V = C₁ + C₂.
items.markingKey: same V, charges add [1]; C = C₁ + C₂ [1] [2]

items.stem: Derive the formula for the combined capacitance of two capacitors in series.
items.answer: Same charge Q on each; p.d.s add: V = V₁ + V₂ = Q/C₁ + Q/C₂, so 1/C = V/Q = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂.
items.markingKey: same Q, p.d.s add [1]; 1/C = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ [1] [2]

items.stem: Capacitors of 10 μF and 10 μF are connected in parallel, and the combination is connected to a 12 V supply. Calculate the combined capacitance.
items.markingKey: C = 10 + 10 = 20 μF. (equation/substitution, then answer with unit) [2]

items.stem: Capacitors of 22 μF and 68 μF are connected in parallel, and the combination is connected to a 24 V supply. Calculate the combined capacitance and the total charge drawn from the supply.
Two capacitors of 10 μF and 15 μF are connected in series to a 15 V battery. (a) Calculate the combined capacitance. (b) Calculate the charge on each capacitor.
items.markingKey: (a) 1/C = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ (method/substitution) [1]; answer 6.0 μF [1] [2] (b) Q = CV, same on each (method/substitution) [1]; answer 90 μC [1] [2]

items.stem: What is the unit of capacitance?
items.markingKey: C = Q/V.

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Capacitors in series all have the same … (b) Which is the definition of capacitance?
items.answer: (a) charge (b) the charge stored per unit potential difference
items.markingKey: (a) The same charge flows onto each plate in series. (b) C = Q/V.

items.stem: Explain why capacitors in series all store the same charge.
items.answer: Charge flowing onto one plate induces an equal and opposite charge on the facing plate; the connected plates of adjacent capacitors form an isolated conductor with net zero charge, so each capacitor carries the same ±Q.
items.markingKey: induced equal and opposite charges [1]; isolated connected plates have zero net charge [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why the charge on a capacitor is described as +Q and −Q, although the capacitor as a whole is uncharged.
items.answer: Charging moves electrons from one plate to the other via the circuit; one plate gains −Q and the other is left with +Q; the net charge is zero. "Charge stored" refers to Q on either plate.
items.markingKey: electrons moved from one plate to other [1]; equal and opposite, net zero [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain your reasoning in each part. (a) Explain why the charge on a capacitor is described as +Q and −Q, although the capacitor as a whole is uncharged. (b) Derive the formula for the combined capacitance of two capacitors in series.
items.answer: (a) Charging moves electrons from one plate to the other via the circuit; one plate gains −Q and the other is left with +Q; the net charge is zero. "Charge stored" refers to Q on either plate. (b) Same charge Q on each; p.d.s add: V = V₁ + V₂ = Q/C₁ + Q/C₂, so 1/C = V/Q = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂.
items.markingKey: (a) electrons moved from one plate to other [1]; equal and opposite, net zero [1] [2] (b) same Q, p.d.s add [1]; 1/C = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ [1] [2]

items.markingKey: Q = CV = 4.70 × 10⁻⁶ × 5.0 = 2.35 × 10⁻⁵ C. (equation/substitution, then answer with unit) [2]

items.stem: Capacitors of 47 μF and 10 μF are connected in series, and the combination is connected to a 24 V supply. (a) Calculate the combined capacitance. (b) Calculate the total charge stored. (c) Calculate the p.d. across the 47 μF capacitor.
Two capacitors of 6.0 μF and 12 μF are connected in series to a 15 V battery. (a) Define capacitance. (b) Calculate the p.d. across the 6.0 μF capacitor.
items.answer: (a) Charge stored per unit p.d. (C = Q/V). (b) 10 V

items.answer: (a) Charge stored per unit p.d. (C = Q/V). (b) 7.20 V (c) 120 μC

items.stem: The energy stored in a capacitor of capacitance C at p.d. V is …
items.markingKey: W = ½QV = ½CV².

items.stem: Use a graph of p.d. against charge to show that the energy stored in a capacitor is ½QV.
items.answer: V ∝ Q gives a straight line through the origin; work done adding charge ΔQ at p.d. V is VΔQ, a strip of area; total work = area of triangle = ½QV.
items.markingKey: straight line V ∝ Q [1]; energy = area = ½QV [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why only half of the energy supplied by a battery while charging a capacitor is stored in the capacitor.
items.answer: The battery supplies QV (charge Q at constant e.m.f. V) but the capacitor stores ½QV; the other half is dissipated as thermal energy in the resistance of the circuit.
items.markingKey: battery provides QV [1]; ½QV dissipated in resistance [1] [2]

items.stem: A capacitor in a laboratory circuit has a capacitance of 470 μF and is charged to 6.0 V. Calculate the energy stored.
items.markingKey: W = ½CV² = ½ × 4.70 × 10⁻⁴ × 6.0² = 0.00846 J. (equation/substitution, then answer with unit) [2]

items.stem: A supercapacitor in a toy car has a capacitance of 2.5 F and is charged to 2.5 V. Calculate the charge stored and the energy stored.

A 10 000 μF capacitor is charged to 6.0 V and then used to lift a small mass with an electric motor. (a) Calculate the charge stored. (b) Calculate the energy stored. (c) Explain why the energy stored is ½QV, not QV.
items.answer: (a) 0.060 C (b) 0.18 J (c) The p.d. rises from zero during charging, so the average p.d. against which charge is moved is ½V.

items.stem: A 100 μF capacitor is charged to 20 V. What energy does it store?
Suggest why capacitors are used in camera flash units rather than connecting the lamp directly to the battery.
items.answer: The capacitor stores energy slowly from the battery and releases it very quickly, giving a large current and high power for a short time that the battery alone could not deliver.
items.markingKey: stores energy then releases quickly [1]; high power / large current [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why a capacitor is not a practical replacement for a battery in a phone.
items.answer: For the same size, a capacitor stores much less energy, and its p.d. falls steadily as it discharges, whereas a battery supplies an almost constant e.m.f.
items.markingKey: less energy stored [1]; p.d. falls as it discharges [1] [2]

items.stem: A capacitor in a laboratory circuit is charged from a variable supply. The capacitance is reduced to one third while the p.d. across the capacitor stays the same. Predict, with a reason, how the energy stored changes.
items.answer: The energy stored becomes one third.
items.markingKey: Using W = ½CV²: energy stored ∝ capacitance; factor = 0.333 = 0.333. 1 mark relationship, 1 mark conclusion.

items.stem: What is the time constant of a circuit with a 100 μF capacitor discharging through a 20 kΩ resistor?
Explain why the current from a discharging capacitor decreases with time.
items.answer: The current is I = V/R; as charge leaves, the p.d. V = Q/C falls, so the current falls; the rate of loss of charge is proportional to the charge remaining, giving exponential decay.
items.markingKey: p.d. falls as charge decreases [1]; I = V/R decreases / rate ∝ Q [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain how a graph of ln(I) against t can be used to find the time constant.
items.answer: I = I₀e^(−t/RC) so ln I = ln I₀ − t/RC: a straight line of gradient −1/RC; τ = −1/gradient.
items.markingKey: ln I linear in t [1]; τ = −1/gradient [1] [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) What is the time constant of a circuit with a 100 μF capacitor discharging through a 20 kΩ resistor? (b) After one time constant, the charge on a discharging capacitor has fallen to about …
Answer both parts. (a) Explain how a graph of ln(I) against t can be used to find the time constant. (b) Explain why a larger resistance makes a capacitor discharge more slowly.
items.answer: (a) I = I₀e^(−t/RC) so ln I = ln I₀ − t/RC: a straight line of gradient −1/RC; τ = −1/gradient. (b) For the same p.d., a larger resistance gives a smaller current, so charge flows off the plates more slowly; τ = RC is larger.

items.stem: Two 10 μF capacitors are connected in series. What is the combined capacitance?
Give a reason for each answer. (a) Derive the formula for the combined capacitance of two capacitors in parallel. (b) Derive the formula for the combined capacitance of two capacitors in series.
items.answer: (a) Same p.d. V across each; total charge Q = Q₁ + Q₂ = C₁V + C₂V, so C = Q/V = C₁ + C₂. (b) Same charge Q on each; p.d.s add: V = V₁ + V₂ = Q/C₁ + Q/C₂, so 1/C = V/Q = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂.
items.markingKey: (a) same V, charges add [1]; C = C₁ + C₂ [1] [2] (b) same Q, p.d.s add [1]; 1/C = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain your reasoning in each part. (a) Derive the formula for the combined capacitance of two capacitors in series. (b) Explain why capacitors in series all store the same charge.
items.answer: (a) Same charge Q on each; p.d.s add: V = V₁ + V₂ = Q/C₁ + Q/C₂, so 1/C = V/Q = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂. (b) Charge flowing onto one plate induces an equal and opposite charge on the facing plate; the connected plates of adjacent capacitors form an isolated conductor with net zero charge, so each capacitor carries the same ±Q.
items.markingKey: (a) same Q, p.d.s add [1]; 1/C = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ [1] [2] (b) induced equal and opposite charges [1]; isolated connected plates have zero net charge [1] [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Suggest why capacitors are used in camera flash units rather than connecting the lamp directly to the battery. (b) Use a graph of p.d. against charge to show that the energy stored in a capacitor is ½QV.
items.answer: (a) The capacitor stores energy slowly from the battery and releases it very quickly, giving a large current and high power for a short time that the battery alone could not deliver. (b) V ∝ Q gives a straight line through the origin; work done adding charge ΔQ at p.d. V is VΔQ, a strip of area; total work = area of triangle = ½QV.
items.markingKey: (a) stores energy then releases quickly [1]; high power / large current [1] [2] (b) straight line V ∝ Q [1]; energy = area = ½QV [1] [2]
